text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- U.S. aircraft maker Boeing granted a licence for heat processing of aircraft components to the Menasco-Krosno plant in southeast Poland, aviation industry firm Menasco-Krosno said.
- Poland's computer hardware and software sales will grow by 500 percent in the next six years to reach $6 billion, the listed ComputerLand software firm's president Tomasz Sielicki said.

- U.S. energy company Enron will build Poland's first gas-fuelled heating and power plant in Nowa Sarzyna, southeastern Poland, on land bought from the ZCO Sarzyna organic chemical plant, the chemical plant's director Wladyslaw Pilat said.

- Pekao SA bank will consider a $100 million credit request by the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard next week, Panorama TV evening news said. The yard's receiver will postpone the lay-off of 3,500 workers until the decision is made, the receiver said.

- Free expansion of international supermarket chains in Poland will give them an 80 percent market share in two years' time, slashing the share of local retail outlets, Poland's cooperative retail distributors' representatives said.
- ABN Amro plans to develop retail banking services in Poland and Hungary, the Dutch bank's board member Jan Tets said.
- Krakow-based Bank Wspolpracy Regionalnej (BWR) bank will conduct Bytom's munibond issue and organise the issue's secondary market, the bank said.
- The TUK SA motor insurance firm has cut Green Card motor insurance policy rates for drivers going to Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech republic by 40 percent, TUK said.

- The Lublin-based Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy (BDKL) and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) have started a firm, SRP Investment I, which will carry out company restructuring of the banks' customers, the banks said.
NOWA EUROPA

- France's Dassault AT and Mera Blonie computer engineering plant will start production of cash dispensers and bank credit card terminals at the Mera plant in Warsaw province. Polish banks will need over 4,500 cash dispensers by 2000, market analysts said.
- Poland's Finance Ministry is considering the appointment of Karol Szwarc, the Nowe Zycie Gospodarcze weekly's editor in chief, as deputy finance minister, the ministry said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Solidarity trade union leaders at the Polar refrigerator plant accused the finance ministry of plans to sell a 67 percent controlling stake to a foreign strategic investor despite and not a 40 percent stake as planned previously.
- Polisa Life insurance company will soon introduce two new individual life insurance policy offers: Polisa 100 Life and Polisa 100 Fund, the company said.
ZYCIE
- The Warsaw-based Agra auction house's sales from 1992 to 1996 reached 750,000 zlotys. Last year Agra sold 220 works of art worth 470,000 zlotys, the company said.
PARKIET
- The listed Agros food processor and trader's net profit in 1997 will reach 57 million zlotys and is set to grow to 110 million by the end of 1999, a report by HSBC James Capel said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
